62/S0.subgoal: Explain why Unity scripting support is needed for customized XR experiences and how to set up a C# scripting environment to create and attach scripts.

62/S1.subgoal: Describe the basic structure of a Unity C# script and how to inspect variable values and console output.

62/S2.subgoal: Explain how Unity scripts use built-in, user-defined, and event functions to control objects and respond to gameplay events.

62/S3.subgoal: Describe how to instantiate prefabs at runtime and use conditional and loop constructs to control script behavior.

62/S4.subgoal: Explain how the Transform property, coroutines, and InvokeRepeating enable timed or frame-based changes to game objects.

62/S5.subgoal: Describe how Unity scripting supports user input and how to build and deploy the system from the Unity editor.

62/S6.subgoal: Explain why external SDKs are needed, how they fit into Unity's layered architecture, and the general steps for integrating a platform-specific SDK.

62/S7.subgoal: Set up, configure, build, and demonstrate a Vuforia marker-based AR sample project that recognizes an image target and displays a 3D model.

62/S8.subgoal: Summarize the main points of the lecture and conclude the session.
